reporting-org.narrative: Obodo Centre for Advocacy and Equal Rights

description.narrative:
There are currently three cases (two active, one concluded) being handled by the Obodo Legal department and which are set out in brief narrative detail below.
Case I: Bullying & Cybersecurity Quick summary: Young queer medical student in Enugu state who has had his nude pictures posted on some social media platforms by a faceless person who also sends messages threatening to “expose” him.
Steps Taken: Conferred with team and with external counsel and filed a police petition at the Enugu State Criminal Investigation and Intelligence Department on the 16th of May 2024. Progress report: Formal statement was written and signed by the client on the 18th of July.
Investigation by the police has commenced
Case II: Discrimination on health grounds; Labour and Employment Quick summary: Young queer fashion designer who was accepted to a fashion program was compelled by contract to accede to a medical check-up that revealed certain information about his health. He was promptly issued with a disqualification notice citing non-compliance with health standards or reasons and offered compensation in lieu of continued participation.
Steps Taken: Conferred with team and with external counsel. Referred the client to external counsel from Heartland Alliance and Minority Watch who have begun to work on the matter.
Progress Report: Counsel has requested supporting information from the client and has completed the initial fact-sourcing stage. Obodo Legal Counsel has engaged in follow-up meetings with external counsel on legal strategy and appropriate legal approaches (Human rights enforcement vs Common Law writ). A demand notice dated 15th July, 2024 has been filed upon the company. On 30th July, 2024, an originating motions for the enforcement of fundamental human rights was filed at the High Court of Lagos state.
Case III: On 25/10/2024, Two trans persons were arrested on a contrived accusation of stealing a mobile phone. The legal officer intervened immediately at the police station where he negotiated with the police to secure their immediate release.
ONE-ON-ONE CONSULTANCY At the end of the liberty workshops, a “legal confessional” is provided for attendees who so wish to have a one-on-one legal consultation with the legal officer. The legal officer has so far provided private legal consultation to a total of 27 persons.
